introduction_markdown: Geology 1 (0555), June 2026, Ordinary Level. Multiple choice question paper, duration one and a half hours. Answer ALL the 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; choose the one correct answer. Mark only one answer for each question.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.

figures.legende: Crystal model with axes +c, +a1, +a2 (prism taller than wide)
Bivalve fossil shell with feature X
Stress/strain curves with points X and Y
Cliff face with igneous intrusion X and legend

incertitudes: Le sujet imprime une formulation alternative (OR) pour les questions 9, 10, 24, 25, 30, 31, 37 et 38 (version avec figure puis version sans figure) : la version avec figure est la question, la version OR est recopiée dans l'énoncé et traitée dans le corrigé ; les lettres de réponse coïncident sauf lecture contraire de la figure.
Questions 30 et 31 : la figure 3 est un dessin à la main ; X est lu comme la fin de la droite raide (rupture fragile) et Y comme le point où la courbe cesse d'être linéaire (limite élastique).
Question 38 : la figure montre une roche ignée basique, aucune option n'en est une ; clé A (seule roche ignée proposée) à relire.

Questions 6, 23, 29 et 44 : clés établies sur le fond (6 : érosion = action hydraulique et corrosion ; 23 : heterolithic unconformity = nonconformity ; 29 : lithosphère ; 44 : Rayleigh), sujet imprimé sans corrigé officiel.
Aucun corrigé officiel : clés et corrigés rédigés, à faire relire par un géologue.

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 27, 33, 43. 27, 33 et 43 : deux réponses défendables (greenhouse vs deforestation ; basalte vs calcaire ; sismographe vs échelle de Richter), clés visées D, A, D.

questions.enonce_markdown: The rumbling of the ground produced by the sudden breaking of rocks in response to geological forces within the Earth is termed:
questions.corrige_markdown: An earthquake is the shaking of the ground caused by the sudden release of energy when rocks break and slip along a fault. The epicentre is only the point on the surface above the focus, a seismogram is the record made by a seismograph, and vulcanicity is volcanic activity. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The sequence of sedimentary rock strata in which oldest layers are deposited at the bottom and younger layers at the top is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: The law of superposition states that, in undisturbed sedimentary strata, each layer is older than the one above it. Fauna succession orders strata by fossils, cross-cutting relationships say a feature that cuts a rock is younger than that rock, and uniformitarianism says present processes explain past ones. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is the natural satellite of the Earth?
questions.corrige_markdown: A natural satellite is a body that orbits a planet. The Moon orbits the Earth. The Sun is a star, the Milky Way is a galaxy. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a body fossil.
questions.corrige_markdown: A body fossil is a preserved part of the organism itself, such as a bone, tooth or shell. A trace fossil records activity (footprints, burrows); a mould or cast is only an impression or infilling left by a shell or body, not the remains themselves. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Minerals having the same chemical composition but different forms are referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Polymorphs have the same chemical formula but different crystal structures, for example diamond and graphite (both C). Isomorphs have similar structure but different composition; pseudomorphs keep the outward form of another mineral. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following are stream erosional processes?
questions.corrige_markdown: The erosional processes of a stream are hydraulic action, abrasion (corrasion), attrition and solution (corrosion). Saltation, traction and suspension are ways of transporting the load, not of eroding. Only option B contains two erosional processes. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is the closest planet to the Sun?
questions.corrige_markdown: Of the four planets listed the order outward from the Sun is Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, so Venus is the closest. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The driving force behind all mass movement processes is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Mass movement is the downslope movement of material under the pull of gravity. Water, slope angle and lack of vegetation only make movement easier or more likely. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the diagram (Figure 1) and answer questions 9 and 10.

![fig-1](gce-ol-geology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

To which system does the crystal model belong?

*The paper prints an alternative wording of this question (marked OR), for candidates working without the figure:* Which crystal system has its crystallographic axis labeled as $a_1 = a_2 \neq c$?  A) Cubic.   B) Tetragonal.   C) Orthorhombic.   D) Monoclinic.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Figure 1 the three axes are at right angles, the two horizontal axes $a_1$ and $a_2$ are equal and the vertical axis $c$ is a different length (the prism is taller than it is wide, with a square base). $a_1=a_2\neq c$ with all angles $90^\circ$ is the tetragonal system.

Alternative wording (OR): Two equal horizontal axes and a different vertical axis is the tetragonal system. (Alternative answer: B.) **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Same figure as question 9 (Figure 1).

![fig-1](gce-ol-geology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

How many crystal edges can be identified on the model in figure 1.

*The paper prints an alternative wording of this question (marked OR), for candidates working without the figure:* How many crystal faces are there in a cube?  A) 2   B) 4   C) 6   D) 8
questions.corrige_markdown:
The model is a four-sided prism with a top face, a bottom face and four side faces: 4 edges on the top, 4 on the bottom and 4 vertical edges, so $4+4+4=12$.

Alternative wording (OR): A cube has 6 square faces (top, bottom and four sides). (Alternative answer: C.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following rocks result from the contact metamorphism of shale?
questions.corrige_markdown: Baking of shale by a hot igneous intrusion gives hornfels. Marble comes from limestone, quartzite from sandstone, and gneiss from regional metamorphism. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A mineral that has a hardness of 7 is;
questions.corrige_markdown: On Mohs' scale quartz is 7. Calcite is 3, apatite 5 and feldspar (orthoclase) 6. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of a rock that shows alternation of dark and light bands is called;
questions.corrige_markdown: Gneiss is a high-grade regional metamorphic rock with gneissic banding: alternating light (quartz, feldspar) and dark (biotite, hornblende) bands. Quartzite is not banded, slate and phyllite are fine-grained and foliated. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The angle formed between an inclined plane and the horizontal is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Dip is the angle between a bedding plane (or any inclined plane) and the horizontal, measured at right angles to the strike. Hade is measured from the vertical; strike is a direction. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The ozone layer is referred to as a layer:
questions.corrige_markdown: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere and absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation. It is rich in ozone, not in carbon dioxide, and it does not stop atmospheric gases. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: that prevents atmospheric gases from reaching the Earth's surface.
in the atmosphere that prevents direct ultraviolent rays from reaching the Earth's surface.
that separates the stratosphere from the troposphere.
that is rich in carbon dioxide and oxygen.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Southern continent which was formed when Pangaea separated into two is called;
questions.corrige_markdown: Pangaea split into Laurasia in the north and Gondwanaland in the south. Panthalassa was the ocean and Tethys a sea. **Answer: A.**
themes: plate tectonics and sea floor spreading

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a feature found within divergent plate boundaries?
questions.corrige_markdown: Where plates move apart, new crust forms at a mid-oceanic ridge. Trenches, island arcs and fold mountains belong to convergent boundaries. **Answer: B.**
themes: plate tectonics and sea floor spreading

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following magma types is the most viscous?
questions.corrige_markdown: Acid (silica-rich, over 65 % $\mathrm{SiO_2}$) magma has long silicate chains and is the most viscous. Andesitic (intermediate) is less so, then basic, then ultrabasic. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a basic igneous rock.
questions.corrige_markdown: Basalt is the basic (low-silica) extrusive rock. Pumice and rhyolite are acid extrusive rocks, granite is an acid intrusive rock. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Metamorphism can be defined as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Metamorphism is the change of existing rocks, in the solid state, by heat, pressure and fluids, which recrystallises the minerals. Compaction and cementation make sedimentary rock; solidification makes igneous rock. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an erosional process that takes place along the river profile?
questions.corrige_markdown: Abrasion (corrasion) is erosion of the river bed and banks by the load. Deflation and sand blasting are wind processes; saltation is a transport process. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select a medium grained clastic sedimentary rock.
questions.corrige_markdown: Sandstone is made of sand-sized fragments (0.06 to 2 mm), i.e. medium grained. Mudstone and shale are fine grained, and limestone is mainly chemical or biochemical, not clastic. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An unconformity formed when sediments are deposited on eroded granite is;
questions.corrige_markdown: When sediments lie on an eroded igneous (or metamorphic) body such as granite the contact is a nonconformity, also called a heterolithic unconformity because the rocks above and below are of different kinds. An angular unconformity has tilted beds below, a parallel one has beds parallel above and below. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the diagram (Figure 2) showing a fossil shell and answer questions 24 and 25.

![fig-2](gce-ol-geology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

To which phylum does the fossil belong?

*The paper prints an alternative wording of this question (marked OR), for candidates working without the figure:* State the phylum to which the fossil bivalve belongs.  A) Coelenterata.   B) Gastropoda.   C) Mollusca.   D) Brachiopoda.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Figure 2 shows a two-valved shell with a hinge line and teeth and two muscle scars: a bivalve, which belongs to the phylum Mollusca. Gastropoda is a class (not a phylum) of the Mollusca, and Coelenterata and Brachiopoda are different phyla.

Alternative wording (OR): Bivalves belong to the phylum Mollusca. (Alternative answer: C.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Same figure as question 24 (Figure 2).

![fig-2](gce-ol-geology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

Identify the feature labelled X.

*The paper prints an alternative wording of this question (marked OR), for candidates working without the figure:* An impression of adductor muscles on a bivalve shell.  A) Muscle scar.   B) Ligament.   C) Pallial sinus.   D) Hinge.
questions.corrige_markdown:
X points to the rounded scar on the inside of the shell near the end of the valve: the impression left by an adductor muscle, i.e. a muscle scar. The hinge is at the top of the shell and the ligament lies along it; the pallial sinus is an indentation of the pallial line.

Alternative wording (OR): The mark left by the adductor muscles is a muscle scar. (Alternative answer: A.) **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following weathering processes is dominant in temperate regions?
questions.corrige_markdown: Temperate climates have many freeze-thaw cycles, so frost action (freeze-thaw) is dominant. Exfoliation is typical of hot deserts and solution of humid regions with soluble rock. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A major cause of global warming.

*Options as printed:* A) Melting of glacier.   B) Afforestation.   C) Deforestation.   D) Greenhouse gas effect.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Global warming is driven by the enhanced greenhouse effect: gases such as $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and methane trap heat. Melting of glaciers is a consequence and afforestation reduces warming. Deforestation also contributes, so the printed question allows two readings.

**Intended answer: D (Greenhouse gas effect).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A metallic deposit that can be exploited for economic benefit.
questions.corrige_markdown: An ore deposit is a concentration of metallic minerals that can be mined at a profit. Gangue is the worthless material in an ore, and a mineral deposit need not be metallic or economic. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What name is given to the outermost layer of the Earth?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Earth's outer rigid shell, the crust with the uppermost mantle, is the lithosphere. The outer core is deep inside; the atmosphere is the gas envelope, not a solid layer. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the stress/strain curves (Figure 3) and answer questions 30 and 31.

![fig-3](gce-ol-geology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

What would happen to the rock at point X?

*The paper prints an alternative wording of this question (marked OR), for candidates working without the figure:* A geologic structure formed by brittle deformation.  A) Fold.   B) Joint.   C) Anticline.   D) Dome.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Figure 3 point X lies at the end of the steep straight line: a rock that deforms elastically and then breaks with almost no plastic strain (brittle behaviour). Beyond X the rock ruptures. The other curve, which bends over and continues to large strain, is the ductile rock.

Alternative wording (OR): Brittle deformation produces fractures such as joints and faults; folds, anticlines and domes form by ductile deformation. (Alternative answer: B.) **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Same figure as question 30 (Figure 3).

![fig-3](gce-ol-geology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

Identify point Y in figure 3..

*The paper prints an alternative wording of this question (marked OR), for candidates working without the figure:* What type of deformation is responsible for the formation of folds?  A) Brittle.   B) Elastic.   C) Ductile.   D) Inelastic.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Point Y is where the curve stops being almost straight and begins to bend: the limit of elastic behaviour (elastic limit), after which strain is permanent. The point of rupture would be at the end of a curve.

Alternative wording (OR): Folds form by ductile (plastic) deformation, where rock bends without breaking. (Alternative answer: C.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify an exogenetic mineral deposit:
questions.corrige_markdown: Exogenetic deposits form at or near the surface by surface processes; a residual deposit (e.g. bauxite, laterite) is left by weathering. Hydrothermal, magmatic and metamorphic deposits are endogenetic (formed within the Earth). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A rock commonly used as aggregate for concrete is;

*Options as printed:* A) basalt.   B) marble.   C) shale.   D) limestone.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Aggregate must be hard, strong and durable: crushed basalt (or granite) is the classic example. Shale is weak and marble is used as dimension stone. Limestone is also crushed for aggregate, so the printed question allows two readings.

**Intended answer: A (basalt).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: engineering geology and quarry site selection

questions.enonce_markdown: The colour of the powdered form of a mineral is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Streak is the colour of a mineral's powder, seen when it is rubbed on an unglazed porcelain plate. Lustre is how it shines and fracture is how it breaks. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The intersection of three or more faces of a crystal produces:
questions.corrige_markdown: The point where three or more faces meet is a solid angle (a corner). The meeting of two faces gives an edge; the angle between two faces is the interfacial angle. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following minerals has the highest specific gravity?
questions.corrige_markdown: Galena (PbS) is about 7.5. Quartz is 2.65, calcite 2.7 and gypsum 2.3. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the diagram of a cliff face (Figure 4) and answer questions 37 and 38.

![fig-4](gce-ol-geology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

Name the intrusive landform labelled X.

*The paper prints an alternative wording of this question (marked OR), for candidates working without the figure:* An igneous intrusion that is discordant to the bedding plane in a formation.  A) Dyke.   B) Lopolith.   C) Sill   D) Phacolith.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Figure 4 the dark basic igneous rock cuts across the dipping beds: a discordant sheet intrusion, i.e. a dyke. A sill is concordant, and lopoliths and phacoliths are concordant bodies in basins and folds.

Alternative wording (OR): A discordant sheet of igneous rock is a dyke. (Alternative answer: A.) **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Same figure as question 37 (Figure 4).

![fig-4](gce-ol-geology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

Which of the following rock types can occur as X?

*The paper prints an alternative wording of this question (marked OR), for candidates working without the figure:* Identify a possible rock that occurs as minor intrusions.  A) Rhyolite.   B) Sandstone.   C) Shale.   D) Limestone.
questions.corrige_markdown:
X is an igneous intrusion, so the rock must be igneous. Sandstone, shale and limestone are sedimentary and cannot occur as intrusions; rhyolite is the only igneous rock offered (the figure shows a basic rock, but no basic rock is in the options).

Alternative wording (OR): Only an igneous rock can form a minor intrusion; rhyolite is the only igneous option. (Alternative answer: A.) **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mount Cameroon can be classified based on its activity as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Mount Cameroon is an active volcano: it has erupted several times in the last century (for example 1999, 2000 and 2012). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cementing material in sandstones.
questions.corrige_markdown: Common cements of sandstone are silica, calcite and iron oxide; iron oxide is the one listed. Clay, mud and silt are fine particles of the matrix, not cements. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Argillaceous sedimentary rocks are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Argillaceous rocks are clay-rich, such as shale and mudstone, so they are fine grained. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an example of a biochemical sedimentary rock?
questions.corrige_markdown: Limestone forms from the shells and skeletons of organisms and by chemical precipitation of calcium carbonate. Sandstone, shale and conglomerate are clastic. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Name the instrument used in measuring the magnitude of an earthquake.

*Options as printed:* A) Seismograph   B) Seismogram   C) Mercalli scale   D) Richter scale
questions.corrige_markdown:
The instrument that records ground motion is the seismograph, and the Richter scale gives magnitude from its records. The Mercalli scale measures intensity, and a seismogram is the record. The question mixes an instrument and a scale, so it allows two readings.

**Intended answer: D (Richter scale).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The last earthquake waves to arrive at a recording station are;
questions.corrige_markdown: P waves arrive first, then S waves, then the slower surface waves: Love waves and finally Rayleigh waves. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The branch in Geology that is related to Physics is;
questions.corrige_markdown: Geophysics applies physics (gravity, magnetism, seismic waves) to the study of the Earth. Palaeontology is related to biology, meteorology to the atmosphere. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Geology - branches of geology

questions.enonce_markdown: What rock type is formed from diagenetic processes?
questions.corrige_markdown: Diagenesis is the set of changes (compaction, cementation) that turn loose sediment into sedimentary rock, e.g. sandstone. Granite is igneous; gneiss and schist are metamorphic. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is responsible for the transformation of sedimentary rocks to metamorphic rocks?
questions.corrige_markdown: Metamorphism occurs when heat and pressure change a rock without melting it. Melting, cooling and solidification are igneous processes. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cluster of stars in the universe is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: A galaxy is a very large cluster of stars (with gas and dust). The asteroid belt, meteoroids and comets are not clusters of stars. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A porous and permeable rock that can store and release water.
questions.corrige_markdown: An aquifer is porous and permeable and yields water. Aquitards transmit water slowly, aquicludes are porous but do not transmit it, and aquifuges are neither porous nor permeable. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following minerals is a silicate?
questions.corrige_markdown: Quartz is $\mathrm{SiO_2}$, a silicate. Galena is a sulphide (PbS), calcite a carbonate and magnetite an oxide. **Answer: A.**
